title: Work with simran
hookLine: the Name runs under the work
tomorrow: what did young Nanak buy with his father's money?

cards: A barista calling out orders, a nurse charting between rooms, a driver merging in the rain: the hands are busy, and underneath, the mind runs on a track of its own.
Usually that track is a playlist, a worry, a replay of something someone said hours ago. It plays whatever it likes. A line in the Granth puts something else on it.

teach.b: It's among Kabir's saloks, on ang 1376, and it's Namdev speaking to his friend Trilochan.

In paraphrase: with your mouth, repeat the Lord's Name; with your hands and feet, do all your work; keep your awareness with the Pure One. That's simran at work. Not a break from the job, and not a reason to quit it.
A second track running under it. Hands on the order, mind with the One.
Now lay this week's road out behind it. The seal: a plate of truth, contentment and reflection, then thanks. The last page, and the whole Guru, walked end to end.
Then a Gursikh's day began. The early hour, kept for the Name first. Ishnaan: clean body, clear mind.
The morning banis, already written, already waiting. And the day's hukam, one line to carry. Every piece of the morning was getting ready for this: the hours when nobody's sitting still at all.

how: Sikhs speak of kirat karo, earning an honest living, alongside naam japo, remembering the Name; some keep simran running quietly through the working day, repeating Waheguru under the breath while the hands work.

o: keeping the Name in mind while your hands do the work
a set prayer read aloud before a work shift begins
taking a break from your work to pray in silence

games.q: the week, back in your hands — tap the pairs.
p: Name in the mouth, work in the hands
one line, carried as the day's order
the early hour, the Name first

s: simran needs a quiet room and closed eyes
Namdev's line puts the Name in the mouth while hands and feet do the work.
the line on ang 1376 is Namdev speaking to Trilochan
it's among Kabir's saloks, near the end of the Granth.
the Granth's hymns close with a plate of truth, contentment and reflection
the Mundavani on ang 1429: the seal.

games.q: a friend says that to be truly spiritual she'll have to quit her busy job for a quiet life. what does the salok on ang 1376 say?
o: hands and feet do the work while the awareness stays with the One.
leave the world and its work behind, and the Name will come by itself.
work hard first; remembering God is for when the working years end.
games.why: Namdev tells Trilochan to do both at once: the Name in the mouth, the work in the hands, the awareness with the Pure One.

practice: Take five breaths with your eyes open, wherever you are, hands on whatever they were doing. On each breath, say Waheguru silently, or just notice the breath going in and out. Then let the sit keep the second track running.

wordCard.voice: Work with simran. Hands on the work, the Name underneath, as Namdev told Trilochan.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: simran, remembrance: keeping the Name in mind.

carryVoice: Your line: remember at work. Mouth, hands and heart, all on the job at once. A week behind you.

sources.ref: Ang 1376 (Salok Kabir: naamaa kahai tilochanaa mukh te raam samhaal; haath paau kar kaam sabh cheet niranjan naal), paraphrased
